items.body:
Oak Furnitureland, the specialist furniture and homewares retailer, has announced plans to open a new showroom in Ipswich this weekend on Saturday 29th August, bringing its collection of stylish, high-quality furniture to even more customers across the country.
Located at Euro Park Retail Park, the 17,000 sq. ft showroom will showcase the retailer’s expanding ‘Whole Home’ proposition, featuring a series of fully styled room sets to help customers visualise looks across living, dining, and bedroom spaces.
The offering will include several new ranges including the Savannah and Corton collections which feature elevated and modern cabinetry designed for the living room, bedroom, and dining spaces such as TV units, coffee tables, and bedframes.
Customers will also be able to try the new Phoenix CineLuxe and Hadley sofas. A high-back recliner, the Hadley is also complete with a USB-C charging port while the Phoenix tech sofa features reclining seats and integrated speakers for a fully immersive experience – perfect for film fans.
The opening has created seven new jobs locally, including roles across sales and showroom management.
Lee Finch, Showroom Manager, said: “The team is really excited to open the doors to our new Ipswich showroom this weekend. We’re looking forward to welcoming customers from the local area and beyond to our store, and our team will be on hand to help you choose the right pieces for your home.”
Alex Fisher, chief executive of Oak Furnitureland, said: “It’s great to be opening a new showroom in Ipswich – it’s an important step as we continue to invest in our network across the UK. We’re really proud of our expanding range of high-quality, stylish furniture – offering great value at outstanding prices, and which is designed to grow with our customers’ homes. We’re looking forward to welcoming people from across Suffolk to the new store soon.”
Last year, the retailer launched its Lifetime Furniture Guarantee, which covers the structural framework of both cabinet and upholstery collections and demonstrates a clear commitment to furniture built to last. Flexible interest-free credit options are also available, making stylish, high-quality furniture for the whole home accessible to even more homes and families
This latest opening takes their estate to 70 showrooms nationwide, as Oak Furnitureland continues to invest in its retail estate while enhancing the experience for customers both in-showroom and online.

items.body:
Aldi has revealed the next 25 locations to benefit from its £300 million investment in upgrading existing stores across the UK this year.
Stores in London, Liverpool, Aberdeen, Sunderland and Bedford are among those receiving refurbishments and other improvements, including more energy-efficient technology.
Five stores – in Stirling, Paisley, Wollaston, Linlithgow and Lewes – will also be extended as part of the investment programme.

items.body:
Online games are meant to be an easy way to unwind, yet they don’t always feel that simple. You might sit down for a quick session and suddenly realise more time has passed than you expected, or you’ve spent more money than you meant to. That slight loss of control can take the shine off what should feel fun and relaxing.
Fortunately, you don’t need to overhaul how you play to fix this. A few small, practical habits can help you stay in charge, so your gaming time feels calm, enjoyable and fully on your terms.
- Set a personal entertainment budget
It helps to decide what you’re comfortable with before you start playing. This step gives you a clear boundary, so you don’t have to think about spending in the moment. For example, you might set aside the same amount you’d usually spend on a takeaway coffee or a streaming subscription.
Planning your budget for everyday costs can help you figure out a simple weekly boundary. This approach keeps gaming in its place as entertainment, not something that competes with bills or essentials. You stay relaxed because you already know where you stand.
- Use promotions wisely (don’t chase them)
Offers can add a bit of excitement, especially when they include free-entry games or small prizes. You’ll often see bingo promotions on leading platforms, and they can be a nice bonus when they match how you already play.
However, it’s easy to get caught up in trying to keep up with every new offer. Instead, focus on the ones that genuinely suit your routine. For example, if you usually play for 20 minutes in the evening, choose promotions that fit into that window rather than stretching your time.
This habit helps you stay in control and keeps the experience feeling light rather than pressured.
- Make the most of in-built controls
Most devices now include simple tools that help you manage your screen time without much effort. Features like Digital Wellbeing on Android phones let you set daily limits or reminders, so you don’t lose track of time.
You might, for instance, set a gentle alert after 30 minutes. This reminder doesn’t interrupt your fun, but it gives you a moment to check in with yourself.
Likewise, app timers can pause access once you reach your limit, making it easier to stick to the boundaries you set earlier. These small controls support your routine without adding extra hassle.
Final thoughts…
When you keep gaming simple, it tends to stay enjoyable. These suggestions work together to support that feeling. Instead of overthinking it, aim to create a space where you can dip in and out, enjoy a bit of entertainment and then move on with your day.
When you feel in control of your time and your spending, online gaming remains an easy, enjoyable way to unwind on your terms – exactly what it should be.

Labour can boost growth at Budget says Asda boss - but it must change tack and ditch heavy high street taxes
- See more This is Money on Google - save us as a Preferred Source
The boss of Asda has warned of a Budget 'tipping point' as Labour has the chance to boost growth instead of squeezing business with even more tax hikes
Allan Leighton also threw his support behind Mike Ashley's scathing remarks on Andy Burnham's plans to revive the high street and urged him against heaping more taxes on larger retailers.
The chairman's comments come as business leaders have started to set out their case to ministers ahead of the October Budget and as he revealed signs of a turnaround at Britain's third biggest grocer.
He said the Budget was an opportunity for the new Prime Minister and Chancellor to shift away from a model of heavy taxes on business which inhibits growth to one that enhances it.
'This is a real tipping point: instead of just talking about growth, the government now has an opportunity to change tack and actually make growth happen.'
Asda boss Allan Leighton has said the Budget will be a 'tipping point' that could set the scene for future economic growth - or result in large firms finding it harder to invest
Leighton added that the next couple of months were 'critical' as consumers' confidence when they return from their summer holidays will 'set the scene for the rest for the year,' including the important Christmas trading period.
It comes as Sports Direct Tycoon Mike Ashley this week said that it would be 'disastrous' to tax larger retailers more in order to fund discounts for other businesses like pubs.
Burnham this week insisted he would 'take pressure off' businesses, which have complained about consumers having less cash to spend while their own operating costs have soared in recent years.
His plans include funding business rates discounts for pubs and clubs by increasing business rates on online retail warehouses as well as tougher rules for vape and betting shops.
Mike Ashley - whose stable of retailers encompasses House of Fraser, Flannels, Sofa.com, Jack Wills and Evans Cycles - said that it would be 'simply delusional' to tax larger retailers more through raising rates further.
He lambasted a 'disastrous' approach to business rates and 'the dramatically increasing cost of employing people' as the biggest obstacles for businesses.
Leighton said that Ashley's comments were 'absolutely right'.
He added: 'All of the things that have been the policy so far have added cost to, not just retail, across the piece. And then that has reduced the profitability of those organisations, and therefore they've got less money to invest in growth. It's economics 101.'
It comes as Leighton hailed signs of a revival at Asda, which has been struggling with falling sales since its takeover by a private equity firm a few years ago.
Sales rose 0.2pc over the seven weeks to 18 August, in a return to growth for the first time in more than two years. Leighton called this 'an important milestone'.
He said the group was 'about a third' of the way through its recovery, which has included slashing prices and a major online upgrade.
But Asda said sales fell 2.3pc for the three months to the end of June, with revenue of £5.1bn.
'I see this really as the sort of foothills of recovery still, but also the foothills of possibility,' Leighton added.
Earlier this year, Asda accounts revealed that pre-tax losses had widened from £599million in 2024 to £989million in 2025, as total sales fell 3.4 per cent to £25.9billion.
Leighton, who rejoined the Leeds-based retailer in November 2024, has warned that his revival plan will not be an overnight fix and slashing prices will hit profits.
But he warned there was pressure on prices due to the heatwave impacting crops this summer.
'The crops are in a tricky state, not just in the UK, everywhere, you know clearly and it's more a produce issue than anything else.'
He said that the grocer had thousands of producers and growers and is 'working very hard with them' to ensure availability 'sticks up as well as we can' and to 'manage the inflation in the best way we can.'
'We generally inflate below the market anyway, so generally when there's high inflation, that's quite a good thing for us.'
He added: 'But the biggest thing is consumer sentiment. How do people feel? Do they feel as if they want to spend? Do they have the money to spend? That's always been the driver of it.'

items.body:
Asda has heralded its first trading growth in more than two years as the supermarket’s boss said it was attracting more shoppers with lower prices and an improved online service.
Allan Leighton, the executive chair of the UK’s third-largest grocer, said a 0.2% rise in sales at established stores, excluding fuel, in the seven weeks to 18 August was “a huge milestone” that was “psychologically important for the business”. In the preceding three months, sales had fallen 2.3%.
“Our price position is strong, we are now getting more customers in the business and we have got some momentum online and that’s been the biggest drag,” Leighton said. The last time Asda’s sales rose was in the first three months of 2024.
He said Asda’s performance had been aided by more stability in its IT systems after a traumatic and expensive shift from the technology of its former owner Walmart. In 2020 the billionaire Issa brothers and the private equity firm TDR Capital bought Asda in a £6.8bn takeover. TDR now controls the business.
Since the buyout, Asda has been struggling with falling sales and profits as well as a huge debt pile, while paying out close to £1bn to revamp its IT systems. Leighton returned to help turn around the business for the second time in his career in November 2024 after a 20-year absence.
Despite inflation on groceries in the UK, Asda’s sales had been falling as the problems with its technology meant it struggled to keep shelves stocked, while it also faced heavy competition from the cut-price chains Aldi and Lidl as well as from bigger rivals Tesco and Sainsbury’s.
Aldi is less than one percentage point behind Asda in terms of market share and continues to grow at a faster pace, threatening to steal its rival’s spot as the UK’s third-largest chain.
Leighton has said it is not inevitable that Aldi will leapfrog Asda, as the bigger chain is fighting back with measures including a deal with the online specialist Ocado to provide technology to improve its website and delivery systems from next year.
“There is some momentum in the business and it is upwards and that is important,” Leighton told the Guardian. He had “never felt not confident” and Asda could be revamped as “the business is too good not to be turned around”.
He said growth had been led by food, sales of which were up 0.7% at established stores during the seven-week period. Sales of clothing and other non-food products fell as, Leighton said, the wider market was tough, and the late August bank holiday had delayed shoppers’ spending on back to school items.
Inflation on food is appearing in some areas of produce, such as tomatoes and cucumbers, as the hot dry summer hit crops, but Leighton said Asda was managing stocks and pricing of petrol well despite high fuel prices linked to the war in Iran. “Produce is the pinch point,” he said.
Leighton said it was not clear if shoppers’ sentiment had improved since Andy Burnham became prime minister, and there was a sense households were waiting to see how things panned out in the autumn and with the October budget announcement.
“People are waiting to see,” he said. “I think John Healey is a good choice as chancellor; he is very sensible and objective.”
But “clarity on the budget and economic plan” would be key to consumer and business confidence, he said. “The key economic policy of the [Labour] government so far has been to inhibit growth.” He wanted to see a minimum policy that “doesn’t inhibit growth and [ideally] enhances growth”.
Leighton added: “That has got to be by not pulling more cost into business.” He called on the government to consider excluding retailers from the additional business rates for larger buildings.

items.body:
Asda in ‘foothills of recovery’ as grocer returns to growth
Asda has posted sales growth for the first time in more than two years, marking a “major milestone” in the turnaround led by Allan Leighton on his comeback at the grocer.
The discount supermarket saw like-for-like sales excluding fuel grow by 0.2 per cent in the seven weeks to mid-August. Like-for-like food sales jumped by 0.7 per cent.
Asda has faced significant market share losses in recent years as it contends with intense competition from German discounters Aldi and Lidl and struggles to boost sales volume.
In November 2024, the grocer called on Leighton to lead its turnaround as chairman. The former Royal Mail and Co-op boss had served as Asda’s chief executive during its 90s heyday and orchestrated its £6.7bn sale to Walmart.
Leighton described Asda’s return to growth as a “major milestone for Asda” following 18 months of “hard work to strengthen our proposition, improving price, availability and the overall shopping experience.
“While this progress is encouraging, we are still in the foothills of recovery. There’s still more work to do as we focus on building a stronger business for the long term.”
Asda also revealed its sales figures for the second quarter of 2026, which saw like-for-like sales fall by 2.3 per cent. Food sales dropped by 1.9 per cent. The grocer increased its total revenue by 0.4 per cent to £6.5bn in the second quarter. This growth has accelerated in recent weeks, gaining 2.1 per cent year on year.
The supermarket’s market share losses have steadied in recent months, with its share holding at 11.5 per cent, according to Worldpanel by Numerator.
Asda battles shaky consumer confidence
Aldi and Lidl have leapfrogged Asda rival Morrisons into the top five in recent months, sitting behind Asda on 10.8 and 8.8 per cent of the market respectively.
Michael Gleeson, Asda’s finance chief, said the grocer is contending with fragile consumer confidence as it battles to boost its market share.
He said: “A challenging geopolitical and economic backdrop continued to weigh on consumer confidence and household budgets during Q2.
“Despite these pressures, our continued investment in price and the overall customer proposition means we continue to make steady progress in our turnaround journey.”
Asda is set to kick off the pilot for its partnership with home delivery firm Ocado before the end of 2026. The group will also roll out a collaboration with Amazon Ad Services later this year, which it says will “deliver a more personalised online shopping experience for customers”.
Private equity firm TDR Capital bought Asda in 2021. The grocer has struggled with a hefty debt pile since its takeover, though its net debt fell from £4.1bn to £3.5bn in the year to December 2025. In the same period, Asda’s pre-tax loss widened by 65 per cent to £989m.

items.body:
October Budget could be a ‘tipping point,’ Asda boss warns Burnham
Andy Burnham’s first Budget in October could be a “tipping point” for British businesses and the economy, the chair of supermarket giant Asda has warned.
Allan Leighton, who is attempting to push through a turnaround of the grocer, said it is “too early to tell” whether the government is committed to halting the rise of taxes facing the UK’s businesses but warned the Prime Minister he must not “inhibit growth”.
“The model so far has been to inhibit growth, which is high taxation of consumers, relatively high taxation and lots of costs being piled on business, and [with] those two things you’ll never grow,” he told City AM.
“For me it’s all to play for. I think [it is a] tipping point. It’ll be a tipping point, the Budget, for consumer confidence and growth of the country.”
Leighton has been critical of previous governments, which he said have been “more and more difficult” to deal with and less supportive of businesses.
The Asda chair said it is “too early to tell” if Burnham will support the growth of British firms. “I’m a bit of a Burnham fan, but that’s another story.
“I think he’s a very shrewd politician, and has announced things that are popular. But that’s not the full answer. The full answer is what’s the economic model for the country.”
Business rates reform would make ‘big difference’
The comments echo an intervention by Frasers Group founder Mike Ashley, who on Thursday accused Burnham of choosing “populist” policies over long-term fixes.
“Rather than address the real underlying issues of how the country’s financial affairs are managed […] it is easier for you to pick topics which provide good media soundbites and the old salve of yet more regulation – which is not what the country needs to become competitive,” Ashley told the Prime Minister in a letter.
The retail tycoon’s letter took aim at Burnham’s “disastrous” position on business rates, and Leighton said that reforms to this tax would make a “big difference” for British firms.
Retailers have urged Labour to meet its manifesto pledge to “replace” the business rates system, but Burnham this week announced a review into the tax which covers only pubs and hotels.
Leighton returned to Asda in November 2024, more than three decades after he first joined the grocer. As marketing director and later chief executive, he overhauled the retailer and orchestrated its blockbuster £6.7bn sale to US retail giant Walmart.
“If I didn’t think we were going to restore the business to what it was, then I wouldn’t be here. So I’m confident that we’re doing the right things, but all these businesses are the same. It’s how you execute in every individual store, every day,” he said.
New Asda CEO ‘not imminent’
Leighton expects his turnaround of Asda to take between three and five years, adding that his previous efforts at the grocer took four.
The grocer is in a “not dissimilar” position now compared to when he first joined the business, though its clothing, petrol and convenience arms “give us another couple channels to fight in,” he said.
Leighton is currently Asda’s sole figurehead as its chair, and he said that the appointment of a chief executive is “not imminent”.
“The preference would be to appoint a CEO from inside the company, and we have a very highly talented group of executives, and my hope is that somebody would emerge from the group.
“But that is not imminent yet because we’re still working with the group that we’ve got to deliver what we’re doing. But that’s the intent,” he said.
Asda returned to growth for the first time in more than two years in the seven weeks to mid-August, with like-for-like sales excluding fuel rising by 0.2 per cent.
The private-equity-owned grocer fell to a £989m pre-tax loss in the year to December 2025, as its debt pile fell from £4.1bn to £3.5bn.

items.title: New plug in solar panels are only being sold by ONE major retailer online from launch day... and they won't be delivered until October
items.summary: Some of Britain's best-known and largest retailers told This is Money shoppers will have to wait to buy plug-in solar panels from their online or high street shops.
items.body:
New plug in solar panels are only being sold by ONE major retailer online from launch day... and they won't be delivered until October
- See more This is Money on Google - save us as a Preferred Source
Plug-in solar panels can legally be sold in Britain as of this week, but customers might have to wait some time to benefit from any sunny weather.
The Government has changed the rules on the sale of smaller, cheaper and more portable panels designed for flats, claiming more people will save on their bills using solar energy.
The devices are allowed to be sold in Britain as of yesterday, August 27 and estimates suggest they could save users £70 to £100 per year on bills.
But some of Britain's best-known and largest retailers told This is Money shoppers will have to wait to buy plug-in solar panels from their online or high street shops.
Argos has put the panels on sale, with a selection of plug-in home kits available priced between £599 and £989.
Argos was the only big-name retailer to start selling the solar kits on Thursday.
Argos' £599 plug-in solar panel kit includes a 515W solar panel, 800W microinverter, hybrid frame and connections. The panels are not suitable for balconies, it said.
From today, Octopus Energy has also started selling plug-in solar panels on its website, with prices from £450 for one panel. Orders will be delivered from the end of September.
On sale now: Argos is selling a selection of plug-in solar panels - but delivery is not quick
Other retailers, such as B&Q, Lidl, Wickes and Amazon, all said the panels would be available to customers at a later date.
And for keen proponents of green energy looking to buy the panels from Argos online or in store today, they will have to wait until October to receive their order.
A spokesman for B&Q told This is Money it 'hoped' plug-in solar panels would be available to buy from its online and physical shops 'from October'.
They added that the chain wanted to ensure the plug-in solar panels it sold were affordable and 'safe, compliant and easy for customers to use'.
Amazon and Currys both said they did not yet have a set date for the launch of plug-in solar panels for the home in Britain.
John Boumphrey, UK & Ireland country manager, Amazon said: 'The Government's announcement on plug-in solar panels is a practical step that gives households a simple way to generate their own power, reduce bills, and contribute to the UK's net zero goals. We're looking forward to helping customers benefit from this technology.'
Wickes is also understood to be preparing to sell the solar panels at some point.
Meanwhile, Lidl said it did not have an update on a potential launch date for plug-in solar panels in its stores.
Across Britain, nearly 172,000 solar installations have been fitted since the start of 2026, the government said this week. Rooftop solar accounted for more than seven in ten installations in July, it added.
Energy minister Michael Shanks said: 'From the South East to Scotland, households across Britain are embracing solar power and taking control of their energy.
'Record numbers of families are installing solar panels to generate clean, homegrown power, helping them cut their energy bills. And through our Warm Homes Plan, we will upgrade homes, tackle fuel poverty and make rooftop solar more affordable for families.
'Now, by making plug-in solar available across Great Britain, we’re making it easier than ever for more families to benefit from Britain’s solar revolution.'
In action: The panels can save users between £70 and £100 per year on bills - but only if they can find somewhere to buy them
Know the risks before buying plug-in solar panels
Plug-in solar panels are cheaper than roof panels, can be installed without an electrician and are suitable for certain properties with outdoor space.
The government said households could save up to £110 a year on their energy bills by using plug-in solar panels at home.
But industry experts have warned that not all properties are ready for plug-in solar panels.
Older wiring, inadequate electrical protection and incorrectly installed equipment can increase the risk of overheating, electric shock and, in the most serious cases, fire.
As demand grows, homeowners should ensure their property is suitable and that any equipment meets safety requirements.
Take steps to ensure your home is suitable for plug-in solar panels:
1. Don't assume every home is suitable for plug-in solar
Experts at Electrical Safety First said: 'Given unresolved concerns about the potential impact of plug-in solar panels on certain residual current devices (RCDs), we recommend households have at least a Type A bidirectional RCD protecting circuits intended for use with plug-in solar panels.
'Until these concerns are addressed, homes with Type AC RCDs should not use plug-in solar systems without first upgrading to a minimum Type A bidirectional RCD on those circuits.'
2. Have your electrics checked before you buy
Do not assume 'plug-in' means it's suitable for every home. It is a good idea to have your electrics assessed by an electrician registered with a competent persons scheme before purchasing or using a plug-in solar system, particularly in older properties or where the condition of the electrical installation and type of protective devices is unknown.
3. Never connect plug-in solar through extension leads or adapters
Plug-in solar systems should not be connected via extension leads, cable reels, multiway adaptors, travel adaptors or plug-in RCD adaptors.
Electrical Safety First said: 'These accessories can overheat, become overloaded and create additional safety risks.'
4. Buy from reputable retailers and avoid third-party sellers via online marketplaces
Experts at Electrical Safety First said: 'Given the size of these devices, it is likely many shoppers will seek to purchase them online.
'We urge shoppers to stick to reputable high street retailers and their online websites to ensure the device they are buying is safe and meets the new interim product specification.
'We advise households to avoid buying these devices from third-party sellers on online marketplaces, no matter how appealing this may be, as these platforms are currently not legally responsible for the safety of goods sold via their sites, exposing people to substandard versions that may put you and your home at risk.'
5. Follow the one home, one device mantra
Only one plug-in solar panel system is permitted per household. Installing multiple units could reduce the effectiveness of protective devices.
Megan Dunford of Zurich UK, said: 'Plug-in solar panels promise cheaper, greener energy, but they shouldn’t be treated like a plug-and-play gadget. Fundamentally, you’re adding a mini power station on your home, so you need to go into it with your eyes open.'
She added: 'If you rent your home, live in a flat, or need to install panels on an external wall, balcony or other communal structure, seek permission from your landlord or freeholder before installation. Solar equipment should also be considered as part of any building fire risk assessment.'

items.body:
How the 'Amazonification' of car buying is helping Chinese brands leapfrog established carmakers we've loved for decades
- See more This is Money on Google - save us as a Preferred Source
Car giants including Volkswagen, Vauxhall and Ford have seen their sales take a hammering in recent years.
But it's not because motorists are falling out of love with the established brands they've known and trusted for decades.
Instead, British car buyers are increasingly choosing their next set of wheels using an Amazon-style approach, and it has helped a fresh wave of Chinese competition thrive.
Research by automotive data technology experts Vehicle Data Global (VDG), exclusively shared with This is Money, has found that almost all motorists now begin their car-buying journeys online, comparing models before visiting dealerships or showrooms.
And previously unknown Chinese brands have been able to gain traction online in much the same way Chinese-made products established their dominance on Amazon.
VDG says the switch to electric vehicles has accelerated this trend.
Operations director Ben Hermer tells us: 'Car buyers are increasingly applying their online shopping habits, developed through buying electronics and household products from unfamiliar online brands on Amazon, to their car-buying process.'
This is Money reveals that British car buyers are choosing their next set of wheels through an Amazon-style approach: Here's how EVs and Chinese brands are hooking motorists online
In the decade between 2015 and 2025, Ford fell from the UK's most popular car brand to third overall.
But that decline is nothing compared with Vauxhall, which has tumbled from second place to 13th.
The former favourites have seen their registrations cannibalised by increasing competition, with sales down 64 per cent and 70 per cent respectively.
Even Volkswagen, last year's market leader, recorded registrations 19 per cent lower than a decade earlier.
VDG's analysis of car brand fortunes over the past two decades suggests the decline of some of Britain's household automotive names reflects a broader shift in consumer behaviour, as researching and shopping online becomes the norm.
In particular, the move to EVs has intensified the pressure on traditional car giants by positioning vehicles more like feature-rich consumer goods, making comparisons easier than ever.
Hermer said: 'Electric cars lend themselves particularly well to feature comparisons in the same way that household and other consumer products are assessed on Amazon, with buyers keen to compare range, charging speed, battery capacity and features such as cabin screen quality and driver-assistance equipment alongside traditional considerations such as warranty length and finance terms.
'This has favoured Chinese manufacturers, who come from an existing culture of providing long lists of standard features, compared with established manufacturers that have tended to bundle many of their most advanced technologies into costly option packs.'
This has enabled relatively unknown brands to compete for attention from the outset on the basis of value.
As a result, motorists are increasingly adopting an Amazon-style comparison mindset when shopping for a car, rather than relying on the brand loyalty that once guided many buying decisions.
Today, the car marketplace is overflowing with unfamiliar but highly specified and affordable Chinese products, mirroring how Amazon changed the way consumers shop
How Amazon-style buying benefits Chinese brands
Back in the sixties and seventies, vehicle choice was largely limited to familiar manufacturers, with many drivers remaining loyal to the marque they had always owned.
Today, the marketplace is overflowing with unfamiliar but highly specified and affordable Chinese products, mirroring the way Amazon transformed consumer shopping habits.
VDG compares the pressure facing car brands and dealerships to the challenges experienced by the High Street in its battle against online retail.
But it isn't the growth in online car purchasing, the most obvious Amazon comparison, that has had the greatest impact on the automotive market, VDG says.
Instead, the bigger influence has been increased competition based on price, specification, availability and digital appeal.
Hermer explained: 'Facing several years of increased living costs, car buyers increasingly favour Chinese manufacturers, which tend to provide long equipment lists and exciting technological features as standard.
'Cars are increasingly becoming bundles of searchable features, which for some buyers may be more important than longstanding engineering pedigree, handling character and brand history.
'As a result, the Amazon-style research process has conditioned many consumers to respond to instantly eye-catching promises, such as "360-degree camera included."'
Many new Chinese car companies are owned by the same parent group despite operating under different brands. One of the most prominent examples is Omoda and Jaecoo, with the latter producing the best-selling Jaecoo 7
Amazon-style brand choice: Not as it seems
In the same way Amazon gives the impression of almost limitless brand choice and competition, many seemingly independent products actually come from the same factories or corporate groups. VDG says the same pattern is now emerging in the car market.
The most prominent example is Omoda and Jaecoo, both Chery brands, with the latter producing the 'Temu Range Rover' Jaecoo 7 SUV. Together, they have sold more than 100,000 cars in the UK despite only celebrating their second anniversary in August.
Similarly, Chinese automotive giant Geely owns famous marques including Volvo, Polestar and Lotus.
Hermer said: 'Although it appears at first sight that car brands are proliferating, they are typically originating from widely shared technology and a relatively small number of platforms, battery manufacturers and parent companies.
'So, while it has often been said that online car buying was the main legacy of Amazon, the reality is that the shift in the car market has been deeper: from a limited choice of familiar brands towards a marketplace filled with unfamiliar but attractive Chinese products competing through price, features, fast availability and digital appeal.
'Marques such as Ford and Vauxhall have therefore experienced dynamics similar to those faced by electronics brands such as Sony and Philips, which have increasingly been challenged for market share by strong value-for-money newcomers.'
Britain stands out in Europe because it chose not to impose duties on Chinese-made EVs, making the UK a much more attractive market for Chinese brands than the EU
Chinese car companies enjoy tariff-free EV sales
Britain stands out in Europe because it chose not to impose duties on Chinese-made EVs, making the UK a much more attractive market for Chinese brands than the EU.
Countries across Europe have imposed tariffs of between 7.8 per cent and 35.3 per cent on Chinese-made EVs in response to concerns that China's EV supply chain benefits from substantial state support.
However, despite these factors, VDG says legacy brands 'still have a real advantage' thanks to their 'expertise in managing the used market, residual values, parts supply and logistics chains'.
Hermer added: 'None of this means that the game is over for the traditional automotive giants, which are still adjusting to the new conditions.
'Just as Amazon's marketplace is characterised by rapid entry, intense price competition and the frequent disappearance of products, we believe that not all of the current Chinese brands will necessarily achieve the scale needed to maintain long-term success.'

items.title: Sports Direct founder attacks Burnham's 'populist' High Street plans
items.summary: In a letter, the entrepreneur accuses the prime minister of "jumping on 'everyday fixes' or bandwagons" with his latest cost of living and retail policies.
items.body:
Sports Direct founder attacks Burnham's 'populist' High Street plans
- Published
Sports Direct founder Mike Ashley has criticised Prime Minister Andy Burnham's cost of living and retail policies as "populist".
In a letter to Burnham, Ashley accused him of "jumping on 'everyday fixes' or bandwagons" while businesses struggled with the government's "disastrous" business rates policies and higher employment costs.
He also described a proposal to increase business rates on large warehouses in order to help reduce rates for pubs and clubs as "delusional".
A Downing Street spokesperson said Burnham would "build a new economy that backs British business, delivers growth in every postcode and ensures the essentials in life... are affordable again"
Removing the VAT from household electricity bills and reducing business rates for some firms was "just the start", the government spokesperson added.
Burnham has promised to revitalise Britain's "hollowed out" High Streets and to address cost of living concerns by tackling "rip-off Britain" including misleading discounting in shops.
Ashley's Frasers Group was built on buying up struggling brands and undercutting rivals on price. It is still owned by Ashley but now run by his son-in-law Michael Murray.
The business currently owns Sports Direct, Flannels, House of Fraser, Game, Evans Cycles, Slazenger, Jack Wills, and Gieves & Hawkes, and several other retail brands.
Ashley's letter, seen by the BBC and first reported by the Financial Times,, external hits out at the government's strategy.
"Shortsighted or populist reactions to underlying business challenges are not the answer. You have the chance to make a difference or get it horribly wrong," he wrote.
He called on Burnham to use his first Budget, scheduled for 28 October, to lower costs for employers and address business rates.
The government has launched a review of the tax on commercial properties, but in advance of that has already announced that pubs, social clubs and live music venues will get a 20% business rates cut from April.
"If your answer is to tax larger retailers even more, through hiking business rates on retailer-owned or third-party warehouses whilst reducing rates for pubs and clubs, then that is simply delusional," Ashley's letter said.
Burnham previously said before he was prime minister that cuts for pubs, clubs and music venues could be paid for by higher levies on warehouses operated by online firms such as Amazon, and targeting the owners of empty High Street properties.
Ashley built Frasers Group from a single Sports Direct store in Maidenhead in 1982 to a sprawling empire of dozens of brands employing 30,000 people.
The billionaire has frequently attracted controversy from investors and the media with accusations over the years of building success by exploiting workers.
In 2016, Ashley admitted to MPs that workers at his Derbyshire warehouse had been paid below the minimum wage and a policy of fining staff for being late was unacceptable.
The business this month bought luxury department store Harvey Nichols and promised a "significant restructuring" of the business.
In his letter to Burnham he asks: "My challenge to you is â how are you going to help with turning Harvey Nichols around?"
He also raises the issue of retail theft which he said cost Frasers Group approximately Â£40m a year.
Frasers Group has also been increasing its stake in menswear retailer Hugo Boss after its initial takeover bid for the German company was rejected.
- Mike Ashley's Frasers offers Â£1.73bn to buy all of Hugo Boss 
  - Published11 June
Referencing comments by Tory peer and former Marks & Spencer boss Lord Rose, who called the government's recent announcements "hot air", Ashley said in his letter "I agree with him".
"It is the disastrous business rates position (which I have raised many times over the years) and the dramatically increasing cost of employing people that are really causing business to struggle," Ashley said.
Ashley said the High Street would be "further devastated" without major reforms, and warned Burnham's suggestion that he will consider further business rates changes in the coming Budget were "too little, too late".
He also used the letter to attack Burnham's plans to clamp down on the use of recommended retail prices, saying instead the real issue is "price fixing in sporting goods and other markets" - where he cited the rising cost of official football merchandise.

items.body:
Clutch VC leads pre-seed investment for new retail media platform Advisar created by Walmart veteran
Advisar, an AI powered decisioning layer for retail suppliers, has raised a $750 million pre-seed round led by Clutch VC, with participation from Venture Center Arkansas Fund, The Validation Fund at Winrock International, Rekall Capital, and White River Capital Advisors, along with angel investors Michael Paladino, Co-Founder of RevUnit, and Jeff Amerine, General Partner at Cadron Capital. The funding will be used for product development and go to market efforts.
Founded by Christina Johnson, former Chief of Staff to the GM of Walmart Connect, Advisar aims to bring clarity and insight to the world of retail media analytics, giving suppliers a clear view of how investment in this space connects to business results. Currently in beta, it lays claim to significant early adoption of its solution among key partners. It is set to become generally available during the autumn.
“Advisar helps suppliers treat retail media like an investment they actively manage, rather than a line item they simply accept,” says Johnson. “What suppliers need is the same standard of measurement they hold every other marketing investment to, so they know what's working, what's not, and where to optimise for efficiency and impact.”
“Every fast growing marketing channel eventually gets an independent measurement layer, and retail media is at that point now. Christina's experience across marketing, customer strategy, and retail media innovation at Walmart positions Advisar to deliver what suppliers have been asking for: attribution insights on retail media investments, integrated alongside all their other sales and marketing metrics,” says Rajiv Bala, General Partner at Clutch VC.

Retail media will be a key focus area at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards.
The awards are now open for entries and celebrate global retail technology innovation in a fast moving omnichannel world.
Our winners will be revealed at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony, taking place at The HAC in Central London on Wednesday, 4th November.

Congratulations to our winners, and a big thank you to our sponsors, judging panel, the legend that is Tiff Stevenson, and all those who attended our 2025 gathering.

Walmart changes Apple Pay stance as Tesco doubles down on robots: this week's biggest retail technology stories
It's Friday, the weekend is almost upon us, so let’s kick back and reflect on another eventful week for the retail tech space. Here's your briefing on the most important stories from the past few days, including Gap Inc., The Home Depot, M&S, Burberry, KFC UK & Ireland, Gatik, Kroger, Instacart, Everseen, Hanshow, OpenAI, and the first ever RTIH Retail Technology Hot 100 List.
1. Justin Breton departs Walmart for Fashiontainment push across Gap, Old Navy, Banana Republic, Athleta
Last week, we reported that Justin Breton had left Walmart, where he spent the past six and a half years, most recently serving as Head of Partnerships, Content & Emerging Experiences.
In a LinkedIn post, he said: “It’s truly hard to put into words just how excited I am for this opportunity. I’ve spent much of my career exploring what happens when brands create experiences people genuinely want to be part of, whether through content, gaming, entertainment, or the unknown.”
“Now, I get to take everything I’ve learned and apply it in an entirely new way: helping develop original content and entertainment for some of the most iconic brands in the world. I’ll be working alongside Pam Kaufman (Chief Entertainment Officer) and an incredible team to dream up ideas, develop them, and help bring them to life.”
He concluded: “I’m grateful to the Gap Inc. team for believing in me. Grateful to everyone who has helped me get here. And incredibly excited to be a beginner again, to listen, learn, meet new people, and build something new and exciting together. One great story with Walmart may have ended, but I have a feeling this next chapter is going to be a fun one.”
2. Tesco extends its UK trial of Simbe's in-store autonomous inventory scanning solution Tally
Last month we reported that Tesco was trialling Simbe’s Tally in-store shelf scanning robot.
Having kicked off with a single store, the pilot is now being extended to a small number of other locations. Thanks to Toby Pickard, Retail Futures Senior Partner at IGD, and a member of the judging panel for the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards, for bringing this to our attention.
In a LinkedIn post, he said: “I’ve now seen Simbe’s Tally robot in a third Tesco store in the UK - another store trialling autonomous inventory scanning. But this time, I had my son with me. His reaction was fascinating. He was completely intrigued by Tally: watching it move around the store, trying to work out what it was doing, and following it with the kind of curiosity only a child can bring to something that feels like it has just stepped out of the future.”
He added: “I’ve heard that in the US, some shoppers will even choose stores specifically because they have Tally, because their children love seeing the robot. Honestly, I can believe it. And it got me thinking…We often talk about retail automation in terms of efficiency, accuracy, labour productivity and ROI. But what happens when the technology itself becomes part of the customer experience? Could robots like Tally become something that customers - and especially children - actively want to see?”
Could, Pickard asked, the presence of robots change which stores people choose to visit? And perhaps more importantly: what happens when the next generation grows up thinking autonomous robots moving around a supermarket is completely normal? Will they see Tally as technology? Or simply as part of what a modern store is?
Pickard concluded: “There’s a fascinating intersection here between automation, operations, customer experience and the psychology of physical retail. I’m increasingly convinced that the question isn’t just, what can robots do for retailers? It’s also, what can robots make customers feel about the future of retail?”
3. Walmart backs down on stand against contactless payments with Apple and Google Pay
Walmart will this week start adding tap to pay options to its checkout stations at US stores and Sam's Club warehouses, with deployment set for completion by end of year. Fuel stations will be upgraded by mid-2027. This includes options like Apple Pay and Google Pay.
Walmart has long resisted the rise and rise of NFC-based payments, opting instead to go all in on its Walmart Pay app and Scan and Go app features for contactless payments.
In a LinkedIn post, Sam Amrani, Founder and CEO at PassBy, said: "Isn't it crazy to think that it's 2026 and Walmart doesn't accept Apple Pay? Until now that is. This has been a case of America's largest retailer vs America's largest consumer tech company."
He added: "Inevitably, Walmart Pay will go down as the largest attempt at creating a closed loop payment system. Its demise will be the final nail in the coffin for retailers trying to create proprietary payment rails for their ecosystem. Ultimately, convenience wins."
"The consumer is the kingmaker, and the result was clear, the convenience of Apple Pay was too important to the customer journey. It will make customers happier and Walmart - although adopting reluctantly - will see this lead to faster transaction times, happier customers and more visits."
4. Nathan Davies swaps financial services for retail as he takes on data and AI role at M&S
Nathan Davies has joined Marks & Spencer as Head of Data & AI Delivery.
In a LinkedIn post, Davies, whose CV includes stints at BlackRock and Lloyds Banking Group, said: “M&S is continuing to scale its data and AI ambitions, and my focus will be on building a strong, predictable delivery capability that helps teams turn great ideas into measurable business impact with clarity, pace, quality, and confidence.”
He added: “What I have seen already is the energy, talent, and ambition across the organisation. I look forward to partnering with teams across data technology, product, analytics, governance, operations, and retail to accelerate delivery while maintaining the quality, governance, and operational excellence required for successful scaling.”
“While I am excited about what lies ahead, I am equally grateful to the many people who have supported me on the journey here. To colleagues, leaders, mentors, friends, and family, thank you. Every opportunity is built on the encouragement, trust, and contribution of others. I have always believed that while individual talent matters, it's teams that win. The best outcomes happen when great people come together around a shared purpose, and I look forward to becoming part of that team at M&S. Excited for the journey ahead and ready to get started.”
5. Kroger connects with Instacart so customers can shop for groceries and prescriptions in a single order
Grocery and prescription delivery is now available across nearly all Kroger banners in the US, including Fred Meyer, Ralphs and Harris Teeter. The Instacart powered capability connects customers to more than 2,200 Kroger pharmacy locations.
Eligible prescriptions are filled and verified by Kroger pharmacy teams before being delivered from the store by an Instacart shopper.
"We're committed to making it easier for our customers to take care of their health and their families," says Colleen Lindholz, President at Kroger Health. "This new service combines the convenience of grocery delivery with the personalised care provided by our pharmacy teams. Customers have groceries and eligible prescriptions delivered together, knowing their prescriptions are filled and verified by the trusted Kroger pharmacy teams who serve their communities every day."
"Grocery delivery has always been about removing friction from people's lives, and picking up a prescription is one of the most important errands customers manage," says Ryan Hamburger, Chief Commercial Officer at Instacart. "Together with Kroger, we're making it easier for customers to access groceries and pharmacy services in one order, bringing greater convenience to everyday life while preserving the trusted pharmacy experience customers depend on."
6. Everseen, Hanshow and OpenAI top first ever RTIH Retail Technology Hot 100 List
In partnership with 3D Cloud, RTIH is pleased to launch its first ever Retail Technology Hot 100 List. We’re bringing you the hottest companies whose solutions and systems are helping drive the retail sector forward.
These companies operate across the omnichannel retail landscape (stores, online, mobile, supply chain, payments etc).
Our judging panel, including Vineta Bajaj, Group CFO, Holland & Barrett, Dan McGrath, JD Group Customer Operations, JD Sports, Dr. Astha Purohit, Director of Product Management, Customer Data and Identity, Walmart, and Paula Bobbett, Chief Data and Digital Officer, Boots, provided feedback on those who have the most innovative, forward thinking technology offerings and are also best addressing retailers' current challenges, painpoints, and opportunities.
The judges used the following framework when making their picks:
1. Retailer problem fit - how meaningful, strategic, and widely felt the retailer pain being addressed is. 2. Production traction in retail (2025–2026) - real named retailer deployments, pilots. 3. Innovation and defensibility - genuine technical novelty paired with a defensible competitive position.
And there was also a public vote, with thousands of members of our community of retail tech enthusiasts getting involved. Thanks to all those who took part! Based on the judging panel's feedback and the public vote, we then drew up our first ever RTIH Retail Technology Hot 100.
So, without further ado, here are the 100 hottest global retail technology ventures right now. Drum roll, please…
7. Autonomous trucking firm Gatik lands $200 million in funding amid growing grocery and CPG supply chain demand
Gatik has announced $200 million in financing as it records increading demand for driverless commercial freight across Fortune 50 retail, grocery and CPG supply chains. The Series D round was led by Qatar Investment Authority (QIA) and Koch Disruptive Technologies (KDT), with participation from Millennium Management, ARK Invest, Intact Private Capital and others.
The capital will be used to expand Gatik's commercial operations and fleet, while it continues to invest in technology, infrastructure and its workforce. It moves freight between distribution centres and stores across Texas, Arizona and Arkansas in the US and in Canada and is targeting more than 100 driverless trucks by the end of 2026.
“This round, led by some of the world’s leading financial institutions, is a clear validation of our commercial leadership in autonomous freight,” says Gautam Narang, CEO and Co-founder at Gatik. “We have built Gatik with real revenue, deep customer demand, and AI driven autonomous technology proven every day in live supply chains. This round gives us the capital to scale with speed and discipline, serve the world’s largest companies, and define the future of autonomous freight.”
“Autonomous freight is transforming the global logistics industry, making it more efficient and reliable,” says Abdulla Al-Kuwari, Head of Industrials at QIA. “QIA is committed to supporting next-generation solutions providers like Gatik that are shaping the future of freight infrastructure.”
8. Jon-Paul Brett swaps fashion for fast food as he exits Burberry and heads to KFC UK & Ireland
Jon-Paul Brett has taken on the role of Chief Digital & Technology Officer at KFC UK & Ireland. He joins from Burberry, where he spent the past ten and a half years, most recently serving as Global Digital Director.
A spokesperson for KFC UK & Ireland says: “Our Original Recipe hasn’t changed. How we run KFC definitely has. Behind the scenes, we’re exploring how AI can empower our restaurants, giving our teams more time to focus on what matters most: our customers and our fried chicken.”
“With 70% of transactions already digital, we’re continuing to modernise our restaurants through new designs, digital kiosks, and digital drive-thrus. Creating a simpler, more convenient experience for customers, whether they eat in or take food to go. So there couldn’t be a better time to welcome Jon-Paul Brett our new Chief Digital & Technology Officer for KFC UK & Ireland.”
They added: “Jon-Paul joined us in July and has wasted no time getting stuck in. He’s been out in restaurants meeting the team members who use our tech every day, while also spending time with our Tech team and franchise partners to understand where the biggest opportunities lie to create best in class experiences for our teams and customers.”
9. Toolstation launches omnichannel gift card programme powered by Edenred Payment Solutions technology
Edenred Payment Solutions (EPS) reports the launch of a new closed loop gift card programme for Toolstation, a UK omnichannel retailer of tools, accessories and building supplies. This enables DIY enthusiasts and trade professionals to purchase and redeem gift cards across all Toolstation touchpoints, including in-store across its network of over 550 UK branches, online, or through the retailer’s mobile app.
Powered by EPS’s API-based payments platform, the programme provides Toolstation with end-to-end card processing capabilities, including real-time top-ups, balance enquiries, and secure redemptions built directly into its checkout systems with zero third-party redirects. EPS also equips the Toolstation team with dedicated customer service management tools and analytics dashboards to monitor activity, breakage, customer behaviour, and campaign performance.
Rehana Mitha, Managing Director at Edenred Payment Solutions, says: "Toolstation is the latest retailer to recognise the importance of incorporating gift cards into their customer proposition. They wanted to create a brand new programme with zero friction when their customers were using the gift card, regardless of how they choose to purchase and redeem across stores, the web and app.”
“They set an ambitious goal of integration, card manufacture, and launch in their stores in just eight weeks. Our dedicated project team worked with great agility and close collaboration with several Toolstation stakeholders to meet this timeline. We are thrilled to support Toolstation with an end-to-end payment solution that promotes long-term customer loyalty while also giving rise to meaningful community and B2B initiatives in the future."
10. Christine Foster departs Kroger Precision Marketing to join The Home Depot's retail media offshoot
The Home Depot reports that Christine Foster will join the retailer as General Manager and Vice President at Orange Apron Media, its retail media arm, effective 8th September.
Foster brings with her 20 years of experience across retail media, digital marketing, content creation and media strategy. She joins from Kroger Precision Marketing (KPM), where she served as Group Vice President of Commercial Strategy and Operations.
“Christine’s deep experience, paired with a proven track record of building high performing teams and driving measurable growth, makes her the right leader to grow Orange Apron Media into an even more powerful engine for our brand partners. I know her vision and leadership will help us accelerate our strategy and unlock new value for the brands and customers we serve. We are thrilled to welcome her to The Home Depot,” says Molly Battin, Chief Marketing Officer at The Home Depot.

items.body:
Marks and Spencer claims an AI first as it deploys animal welfare monitoring tools across dairy farms
M&S says it has become the first retailer to use AI powered monitoring systems on its entire Milk Pool to monitor animal welfare across 46 dairy farms. The tools use cameras to capture footage of dairy cows when they are indoors which is then analysed using an algorithm trained alongside vets to monitor welfare of dairy cows in real-time.
The technology uses AI powered video analytics to build an individual health profile for each animal, tracking mobility and body condition scoring over time to give farmers objective, consistent data on the wellbeing of their herd. The tools monitor the cow’s behaviour including lying time, feeding time, social interactions and mobility to generate a ‘cow comfort score’ which supports vets in their assessment of individual cow’s health. The cameras will assess body condition scoring to assess cows’ nutritional status over time.
Terry Canning, CEO of Cattle Eye says “Changes in body condition are early indicators of metabolic health, fertility, and overall wellbeing. Tracking those changes more regularly, across every cow, gives farmers a level of insight that was previously unavailable outside research environments.”
The algorithm supporting the tool has been tested and, according to those involved, found to perform to the same standard as a trained welfare assessor.
The tools are being rolled out following trials at a selection of M&S dairy farms, where farmers have used the technology to make changes to tailor care to individual cow’s needs. By measuring lying times, farmers have made changes to the bedding of individual cows to improve their comfort based on their specific size and shape. Feeding schedules have been adapted to reduce the amount of time cows spend standing and the design of some stalls has been adapted to improve cow comfort.
Peter Kennedy, Head of Agriculture at M&S Food, says: “M&S has always had market leading welfare standards, and as we continue to support British farmers in this latest evolution of welfare monitoring, powered by AI, it will support farmers to give the best care to dairy cows. Pacsun has announced the second cohort of its Youth Council and the launch of a new Ambassador Programme, with the aim of expanding opportunities for Gen Z and Gen Alpha to directly shape the brand. Poles apart: European hotspots for returns fraud revealed as retail systems struggle to keep up
New analysis from ReBound Returns flags the European markets where retailers are currently most exposed to returns fraud, with Poland recording the highest average fraud rate of countries in the region.
Its data, analysing millions of returned items, showed that one in ten of returned items in Poland were flagged as potentially fraudulent. The Isle of Man followed at 8%, with Hungary and Greece both recording a rate of 7%.
In 2025, July saw the biggest spike in returned items outside of peak season. As return rates grow, the impact of returns fraud scales with it. Previous analysis by ReBound highlights how scaling up also increases potential losses from returns fraud: A mid-market fashion retailer with £100 million in annual sales, a 20% return rate, and a 5% fraud rate would face a projected loss of £1 million each year to fraudulent returns; For a large omnichannel retailer with the same fraud rate, the loss would rise to £3.5 million annually. At enterprise scale, with £960 million in sales and a 7% fraud rate, the projected loss reaches £20 million a year.
ReBound’s data of one million returned orders on behalf of retail clients between July 2025 and May 2026 found £29 million of potentially fraudulent returns.
Liselotte Reijrink, Sales Director UK & EU at ReBound Returns, says: “Pressure to refund quickly has pushed retailers into a ‘refund first, ask questions later’ approach that leaves them exposed to returns fraud. A blanket tightening of returns policies then risks punishing genuine loyal customers who would otherwise have been repeat buyers. Whichever way you look at it, brands are facing potential losses of millions each year caused by returns fraud, and most have no way of knowing how exposed they really are.
“Most returns systems have limited ability to flag risk before a refund is issued. By combining behavioural analysis and risk scoring at the point a return is initiated, with physical verification in regional hubs and connected data across every channel, retailers can catch fraudulent activity before it becomes a loss. This matters even more for international returns when verifying items gets harder when items need to cross borders.”
“If brands don’t have local warehouses or verification hubs, it can take days to assess a return, and brands don’t want to risk delaying the customer refund while the item is verified. Location can be a useful signifier within that model, but local fraud rates can shift dramatically and need to be considered alongside various other returns red flags.”

items.body:
Spider-Man spins a buoyant bricks and mortar web: presenting the retail technology week in numbers
Do you like numbers? Do you like retail technology news? Then this is the article for you. Including eComID, Gatik, Landsec, Mulberry, GoWish, California Pizza Kitchen, Walmart, Levanta, Everseen, Hanshow, Vusion, Sitoo, Simbe, and first ever Retail Technology Hot 100 List.
$17 million...Swedish startup eComID has announced a $17 million seed round led by Systemiq Capital, with participation from Regeneration.VC, Course Corrected, Stadium and returning investor CapitalT. The funding will go towards international expansion, product and team development.
eComID’s Shopping Passport lets shoppers carry relevant context across connected brands, helping each store understand them from the first visit. Vera, the company’s AI shopping agent, combines that context to power sizing intelligence, smart conversational search and personalised product discovery directly on brands' own sites.
Launched in 2024, eComID now works with more than 60 brands and reaches 20 million shoppers every month. Partners include COS, J.Lindeberg, Axel Arigato, NN07, Peak Performance, Haglöfs, Asket and Stadium. eComID was also named one of Fast Company's Most Innovative Companies of 2025.
"AI without context still starts from zero," says Oscar Rundqvist, Co-founder and CEO at eComID. "The best shopping experience should feel like walking into a store that already knows how to help. We're building the missing layer between shoppers, brands and AI to make that possible. We've reached this point through the strength of the product and the trust of our partners. This round lets us move faster, enter new markets and build the infrastructure we believe the next era of commerce will run on."
100...In partnership with 3D Cloud, RTIH is pleased to launch its first ever Retail Technology Hot 100 List. We’re bringing you the hottest companies whose solutions and systems are helping drive the retail sector forward.
These companies operate across the omnichannel retail landscape (stores, online, mobile, supply chain, payments etc).
Our judging panel, including Vineta Bajaj, Group CFO, Holland & Barrett, Dan McGrath, JD Group Customer Operations, JD Sports, Dr. Astha Purohit, Director of Product Management, Customer Data and Identity, Walmart, and Paula Bobbett, Chief Data and Digital Officer, Boots, provided feedback on those who have the most innovative, forward thinking technology offerings and are also best addressing retailers' current challenges, painpoints, and opportunities.
The judges used the following framework when making their picks:
1. Retailer problem fit - how meaningful, strategic, and widely felt the retailer pain being addressed is.
2. Production traction in retail (2025–2026) - real named retailer deployments, pilots.
3. Innovation and defensibility - genuine technical novelty paired with a defensible competitive position.
And there was also a public vote, with thousands of members of our community of retail tech enthusiasts getting involved. Thanks to all those who took part! Based on the judging panel's feedback and the public vote, we then drew up our first ever RTIH Retail Technology Hot 100.
So, without further ado, here are the 100 hottest global retail technology ventures right now. Drum roll, please…
979...Landsec has secured Mulberry at Liverpool ONE. Opening in November, the retailer’s new 979 sq ft store will occupy a prominent position in Keys Court on Peter’s Lane.
It says that the signing reinforces Peter’s Lane’s growing appeal as a premium fashion and lifestyle destination, building on recent leasing momentum with brands including ARNE, Monica Vinader and Salomon’s first full price UK store outside London. It also aligns with Mulberry's ‘Back to the Mulberry Spirit’ strategy, which places renewed emphasis on investing in its core UK market, strengthening customer connection and focusing on the locations best placed to support long-term growth.
Pablo Sueiras, Head of Retail and Hospitality Leasing at Landsec, says: “Mulberry’s decision to open in Liverpool ONE reflects the opportunity presented by Peter’s Lane as it continues to establish itself as a premium retail destination. As the brand sharpens its focus on its core UK market, Liverpool ONE offers the right combination of brand performance and spend potential to support its long-term ambitions.”
73.5%...Spider-Man: Brand New Day, which was released in the UK at the end of July, drove an immediate and sustained uplift in footfall at GRID Braehead in Scotland, which combines experiential activities, dining, cinema and family entertainment. On the film's opening day (Wednesday, 29th July), GRID recorded a +73.5% increase in footfall YOY, replicating similar visitor patterns to a Saturday at the destination.
It also reports positive daily year-on-year footfall uplift through to Monday, 10th August, with the period delivering a +28% increase compared with the same period last year. Many of GRID’s F&B, leisure and retail offerings benefited from the increased footfall as a direct result from the new film release.
According to GRID, these figures underline the important role that entertainment, leisure and shared cultural moments play in driving traffic to retail destinations. For landlords and occupiers, major releases can create a halo effect extending beyond the cinema itself, bringing significantly larger audiences into destinations and creating opportunities for retail, F&B and other leisure operators to benefit from increased dwell time and cross-visitation.
€13.4 million...Social shopping platform and wishlist app GoWish, known as Ønskeskyen in its native Denmark, has secured a capital injection of €13.4 million from various new investors, including Weco owner Johan Wedell-Wedellsborgand and former EQT partner Mads Ditlevsen. The investment values GoWish in excess of $200 million and will be used to accelerate the company’s international growth, with a particular focus on the US, where GoWish has more than nine million registered users.
"We have proven that GoWish can grow far beyond Denmark, and the United States is our largest market today. We are also proud to have some of Denmark's most experienced investors behind our ambition: to build a Danish born company into a global leader in social shopping. This new capital will be used to invest even more aggressively in our international growth, particularly in the US, a key priority on our own wishlist,” says Mads Dahlerup, CEO and Co-founder at GoWish.
100...Walmart has opened its 100th company (across 20 states) owned electric vehicle fast charging site Supercenter in Monument, Colorado.
These are positioned near store entrances, and customers can manage charging sessions through the Walmart mobile app. Walmart+ members receive discounted charging rates. The US retail giant plans to add additional payment options as the network expands.
“By expanding EV fast charging at Walmart locations across the country, we’re giving drivers a dependable way to charge while they’re in the store,” says Shayne Wahlmeier, Senior Vice President at Walmart Energy. “Reaching 100 sites is an important milestone, and our broad footprint positions us to make EV charging more accessible for communities while expanding the ways we serve our customers.”
Most locations feature 8 to 16 fast-charging stalls, with chargers capable of delivering up to 400 kW of power. With both CCS and NACS connectors, the network is compatible with most EVs on the road today.
$200 million...Gatik has announced $200 million in financing as it records increading demand for driverless commercial freight across Fortune 50 retail, grocery and CPG supply chains. The Series D round was led by Qatar Investment Authority (QIA) and Koch Disruptive Technologies (KDT), with participation from Millennium Management, ARK Invest, Intact Private Capital and others.
The capital will be used to expand Gatik's commercial operations and fleet, while it continues to invest in technology, infrastructure and its workforce. It moves freight between distribution centres and stores across Texas, Arizona and Arkansas in the US and in Canada and is targeting more than 100 driverless trucks by the end of 2026.
“This round, led by some of the world’s leading financial institutions, is a clear validation of our commercial leadership in autonomous freight,” says Gautam Narang, CEO and Co-founder at Gatik. “We have built Gatik with real revenue, deep customer demand, and AI driven autonomous technology proven every day in live supply chains. This round gives us the capital to scale with speed and discipline, serve the world’s largest companies, and define the future of autonomous freight.”
“Autonomous freight is transforming the global logistics industry, making it more efficient and reliable,” says Abdulla Al-Kuwari, Head of Industrials at QIA. “QIA is committed to supporting next-generation solutions providers like Gatik that are shaping the future of freight infrastructure.”
1,000...California Pizza Kitchen is set to roll-out up to 1,000 automated pizza making kiosks across the US through a partnership with T-ROC Global. The pair will target real estate with high foot traffic, like hospitals, hotels, campuses, and sports venues, where opening a full sized restaurant would be impractical.
The offering will use TurboChef powered cooking, touchscreen technology and data driven systems. According to California Pizza Kitchen, the kiosks can prepare a pizza in as little as 90 seconds. The menu is expected to extend beyond pizza. Plans are afoot to offer items including Kung Pao and Bolognese spaghetti, Mac ‘N’ Cheese varieties and the brand’s Butter Cake.
California Pizza Kitchen began testing automated retail in 2025. Machines are now operating at airports including Boston Logan International Airport, Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport, Dallas Love Field and Dayton International Airport. The company also expects to activate another 15 at universities by the end of 2026.
“For decades, CPK has been dedicated to meeting consumers wherever they are, whether through our global restaurant network, airport and non-traditional locations, off-site events, or the local grocery store where we’ve been a leading premium pizza brand for 25 years,” says Michael Beacham, President at California Pizza Kitchen Global. “Our automated retail strategy, now accelerated through a partnership with T-ROC, introduces CPK to entirely new occasions and venues where consumers desire quality food on the go.”
100...Wingstop has opened its 100th site across the UK and Ireland. This is located in Inverness, Scotland. It aims to launch up to 30 sites across England, Scotland, Wales and Ireland this year. The fast food chain recently revealed that new stores helped revenues surge by 73% to £216.4 million in 2025.
Chris Sherriff, Chief Executive at Wingstop UKI, said: “Customers increasingly seek out brands that offer a memorable experience, differentiated products and genuine value. To have achieved record results, despite the well reported headwinds facing the broader hospitality sector, is a fantastic achievement.”
In a LinkedIn post, Sheriff added: "I'm incredibly proud to have reached our 100th opening and even prouder of the 3,500+ team and partners who have made this journey possible - from construction, suppliers, events and everything in between. Every opening, every event and every contribution matters. Thank You to the entire team."
He added: "The journey doesn’t stop here.....we’re excited to welcome our new team in Poland as we continue to bring Flavour to new markets. I have so many fond memories over the last five years and can't wait to make many more....here's to the next 100+ sites."
$22 million…Levanta, whose technology helps brands find creators, send them products, set up affiliate commissions, track sales and handle payments, has announced a $22 million Series B investment led by Volition Capital, marking the firm's second major investment in the company after leading its $20 million Series A in 2024.
Levanta has now raised more than $43 million in total funding. The new capital will support investment in creator commerce technology and go to market activity, while accelerating its expansion across the retail ecosystem, including bringing dozens of additional retail marketplaces onto the platform.
"We're seeing a broader shift as brands and marketplaces increasingly look to creators and affiliates as measurable drivers of demand beyond their owned channels," says Larry Cheng, Founding Partner at Volition Capital. "Levanta has built the infrastructure to connect that demand with commerce at scale, and we believe the opportunity ahead is substantially larger than when we first invested. We're excited to continue partnering with Ian and the team as they deploy that infrastructure across the retail ecosystem to power creator commerce media."
$3.2 million...A computer vision company selected into NBA Launchpad 2026 has announced $3.2 million in pre-seed funding and opened its seed round. Swish Basket was founded by Joel Bar-El, who built Trax, a Singapore born startup valued at over $3 billion at its peak.
The pre-seed was led by Aristagora VC, which holds a board seat, with participation from Peter Kadas, Nika Capital, and RGE Group. The funding will support Swish's first commercial installations internationally, expand its sensor and AI engineering team, and launch its US marketing and community building.
Swish's AI sensor mounts above the basketball hoop and uses cameras and lidar to track every shot for accuracy, arc, and mechanics, with instant feedback, no wearables, and no setup. At the heart of the platform is Swish's computer vision technology, enabling facial recognition and real-time player identification. Players download an app, which connects them to their Digital Player Profile and brings every on-court session into one connected experience.
